Senses.Explanation: Literally, a golden body one zhang and six chi tall: the monumental bodily form of a buddha in the records. Chan repeatedly deploys it in a reversible formula: take one blade of grass and make it a sixteen-foot golden body, then make the golden body into one blade of grass. Other passages put the body on a refuse heap, ask directly 'what is the sixteen-foot golden body?' and answer with the administrative phrase 'the judge decides the case; the minister amends it,' or call it a mass of merit that is casually waved into the red dust. The Chan-specific bend is the contrast and reversibility: the exalted buddha-form is repeatedly exchanged with grass or located amid refuse and ordinary dust. These are the corpus's stated comparisons; the texts give no further gloss here.
Senses.Note: Wave-plan frequency: 373. Searches covered the grass reversal, refuse-heap placement, direct interview question, verse deployment, and the family terms a single blade of grass (一莖草), golden body (金身), buddha-body (佛身), and buddha (佛). One referent—the monumental golden buddha-body—appears in all deployments; comparisons do not create senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 便能拈一莖草。作丈六金身。將丈六金身。却作一莖草。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The central reversible formula makes the golden body from one blade of grass and the blade from the golden body.

Occurrences.Kwic: 糞掃堆頭現丈六金身，且拈在一邊
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Old Cases Raised in the Lineage (宗門拈古彙集), Sengcan section. Xuedou Chongxian is the exact commentator who places the sixteen-foot golden body on top of a refuse heap and then sets that formulation aside.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是丈六金身。師曰。判官斷案相公改。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: an unnamed questioning monk is the exact actor. Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Raoshan Heshang section. The headword occurs in an unnamed monk's exact question, 'What is the sixteen-foot golden body?'; Raoshan answers with the judge and minister line. All six rungs leave the monk unnamed.

Occurrences.Kwic: 百草頭上無邊春信手拈來用得親丈六金身功德聚等閑擺手入紅塵
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 禪宗頌古聯珠通集, verse on the Dipamkara ground-marking case. Hongzhi Zhengjue is the exact verse author: the source's inline attribution at the end of this individual verse is 天童覺, and the stored phrase occurs wholly inside that verse.
